passage: By nine, Sameer and Uma were talking over each other about whether Sameer's mother should move in with them. Voices rose. Uma stood at the sink, gripping a plate. Sameer felt his jaw tighten and heard himself say something sharp. He stopped. "This is going badly. Let's stop and pick it up tomorrow evening, after dinner." Uma looked at him for a long moment, then nodded. Nothing more was said that night; they watched an old film side by side, not touching. The next evening, tea in hand, they began again, more quietly. Uma said what she was afraid of: losing the quiet of the flat. Sameer said what he was afraid of: not being there for his mother. By ten they had a plan of three months, with a review at the end. Neither felt they had won.

qa.q: When did Sameer and Uma agree to continue the talk?

qa.a: Uma was afraid of losing the quiet of the flat.

qa.q: What could they do if the second talk also gets heated?
qa.a: They could pause again and carry on another day, since a hard conversation can be split across several days.

qa.q: How might Sameer's mother feel about the plan?
qa.a: Sameer's mother may feel relieved to be wanted, and perhaps a little worried about being a burden.

grounding: When the first talk becomes heated, Sameer says to continue tomorrow, and the calmer second talk reaches a plan.

passage:
"You always do this, Vijay Dada. You decide, and I adjust."
"I decide because you never do! Someone has to be with Baba."
"And that someone is always me, because I'm younger?"
"Because you're closer! Pune to Nagpur is..."
Chaitanya held up a hand. His heart was pounding. "Stop. We're both shouting. Let's finish this tomorrow, same time. I don't want to say something I'll regret."
"...Fine. Tomorrow."
Next evening, 8 pm, video call.
"I slept badly," Vijay admitted. "I'm sorry for 'someone has to'. You're right, I've been deciding."
"I'm sorry too. I've been making you the villain. Here's what I thought overnight: we take turns. Two months each, and we hire a day attendant for the gaps."
"Two months each. I can ask for remote work in January."
"And we tell Baba together, on Sunday."
"Together. Yes."

qa.q: What time was the next evening's video call?
Why did Chaitanya stop the argument?
qa.a: His heart was pounding and he was afraid of saying something he would regret, so he chose to pause.

qa.q: What did pausing overnight make possible?
qa.a: Both came back calmer and apologised, then agreed to take turns two months each with a day attendant, and to tell Baba together.

qa.q: How did Vijay feel after the night's pause?
qa.a: Vijay slept badly but felt sorry and could admit he had been deciding for both.

grounding: It shows a young man stopping a heated talk and continuing the next day, when both brothers are calmer and reach a plan, so a hard conversation spans two days.

passage:
The first time Salma and I talked about moving in with my parents after Abbu's retirement, it went badly. She said she would lose all privacy. I said she was being unfair to people who had only been kind to her. By ten o'clock we were both loud and saying things we didn't mean.
I heard myself start a sentence about her mother and stopped. "Salma, let's continue this tomorrow. I'm too angry to be fair right now." She looked surprised, then nodded.
The next evening we walked to the lake instead of sitting at the table. I had slept on it; so had she. She said her real fear was losing our Sunday mornings. I said mine was Ammi feeling abandoned. By the time we got back, we had a plan: a flat in the same building as my parents, not the same flat.
Two conversations. One plan.
— Imran

qa.q: Where did they walk the next evening?
Why did Imran stop mid-sentence and suggest continuing tomorrow?
qa.a: Imran felt too angry to be fair and was afraid of saying something hurtful about Salma's mother.

qa.q: What made the second talk work?
qa.a: Both had slept on it, they talked while walking instead of across a table, and each named their real fear.

qa.q: How did Salma see the idea of moving in at first?
qa.a: Salma was worried about losing all privacy, and underneath that, their Sunday mornings together.

grounding: It shows a heated first talk being paused until the next day, when both are calmer and reach a plan, so a difficult conversation is spread over two days.
